levels.label: א
levels.name: Alef
levels.guidance: Write for a beginner Alef reader who can decode unpointed Hebrew, not an end-of-Alef graduate. Use familiar concrete words, explicit subjects, and one simple clause per sentence. Prefer present tense in fictional situations; use familiar simple past or future only when the facts or practical exchange require it. Avoid passive forms, abstract action nouns, construct chains, embedded clauses, and several verb forms in one sentence. Prefer repeating a clear noun to an ambiguous pronoun. Introduce only a few necessary unfamiliar terms in the whole article and explain each immediately with familiar words. Do not cluster new vocabulary. Keep adult, natural Hebrew. Difficulty is determined by wording and grammar, not word count. Keep the central situation, required facts, useful answer, and outcome; omit optional names, dates, and technical detail. A shorter clear article is preferable to a dense four-paragraph retelling.

levels.label: א+
levels.name: Alef Plus
levels.guidance: Write for advanced Alef. Use a broader but still common vocabulary than Alef, past and future forms where natural, simple cause and effect, everyday connectors, common fixed expressions, and occasional short subordinate clauses. Keep the story easy to follow. Difficulty is determined by wording and grammar, not word count. Connect familiar ideas with כי, אבל, אז, אם, and short clauses with ש when natural. Introduce a few less familiar words in clear context, without piling them into the same sentence. Keep the same useful answer, outcome, and memorable detail as the other levels.

levels.label: ב
levels.name: Bet
levels.guidance: Write reasonably natural contemporary Hebrew for a Bet learner. Use a wider everyday vocabulary, more precise verbs and adjectives, natural connectors, comparisons, reactions, common colloquial constructions, and moderately more complex sentences than Alef Plus. Avoid dense journalistic syntax and specialist vocabulary. Difficulty is determined by wording and grammar, not word count. Use connected sentences to explain reasons, contrasts, intentions, and reactions. Richer Hebrew should sound conversational, not more official: do not replace ordinary verbs with bureaucratic noun phrases just to raise the level. Keep the same useful answer, outcome, and memorable detail as the other levels.
